title: Pizza with cheese and vegetables, thick crust

content.title: About
content.content: Pizza with cheese and vegetables on a thick crust is a fast‑food dish made from dough topped with tomato sauce, melted cheese, and a variety of vegetables (tomatoes, bell peppers, onions, mushrooms, etc.). The dough forms a dense, crunchy crust while the topping stays juicy and flavorful.

content.title: Interesting Facts
items: Thin and thick crust pizzas differ in dough hydration and baking time.
Mozzarella cheese, commonly used on pizza, was first cultivated in Italy in the 12th century.
Adding vegetables makes the pizza more nutritious and lowers its calorie density compared to meat‑heavy versions.
Pizza gained massive popularity in the United States after World War II when American soldiers brought it back from Italy.
Traditional Neapolitan pizza is baked at 430–480 °C, but thick‑crust pizzas often use lower temperatures and longer bake times.

items.title: Rich source of calcium
items.content: The cheese provides calcium, essential for strong bones and teeth.

items.title: Vitamins and antioxidants
items.content: Vegetables such as tomatoes and peppers supply vitamin C and lycopene, which protect cells from oxidative stress.

items.title: Protein
items.content: Cheese and some vegetables (e.g., peas) add both dairy and plant protein to the meal.

items.title: Dietary fiber
items.content: Vegetables and whole‑grain dough (if used) increase fiber content, supporting digestion.

items.title: Sustained energy
items.content: The thick crust provides complex carbohydrates that keep you feeling full longer.

items.title: High calorie content
items.content: Thick crust and cheese make the pizza calorie‑dense; portion control is advisable for weight‑management diets.

items.title: Saturated fats
items.content: Cheese contains saturated fats, which can raise cholesterol levels if consumed in excess.

items.title: Sodium
items.content: Tomato sauce and cheese are often salty, which may be a concern for people with hypertension.

items.title: Milk protein allergy
items.content: Individuals allergic to dairy or lactose intolerant should choose dairy‑free cheese alternatives.

items.title: Gluten
items.content: Traditional dough contains gluten; those with celiac disease need a gluten‑free version.

content.title: How to Eat
content.content: Serve the pizza hot, cut into slices. It pairs well with a light salad or a drizzle of chili sauce. Fresh herbs such as basil or oregano can be added after baking for extra aroma.

content.title: Storage
content.content: Store leftovers in an airtight container in the refrigerator for up to 2–3 days. Reheat in an oven or grill to keep the crust crisp.
